rules.title: AB 325 Cartwright Act: violations (Bus. & Prof. Code 16729, 16756.1)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term. A common pricing algorithm is any methodology used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term.
rules.key_value: Common pricing algorithm = two or more users and use of competitor data; criminal fines up to $6 million for businesses and $1 million for individuals; civil fines up to $1 million
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm, not limited to housing.
rules.citation: Assembly Bill No. 325, Chapter 338; Business and Professions Code Section 16729
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

rules.title: Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S. amending Berkeley Municipal Code Chapter 13.63 – Prohibition on the Sale or Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents or Manage Occupancy Levels for Residential Dwelling Units
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or provide to Berkeley landlords a coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels, and unlawful for landlords to use one when setting rents or occupancy for residential units. Each month and each unit is a separate violation; the City Attorney and aggrieved tenants may sue.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to coordinated pricing algorithms used or sold for residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated anonymous rental data reports, affordable-housing rent/income limit tools, and market research, appraisal or software development uses.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code Chapter 13.63; Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. 
B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.

rules.exemptions: Golden duplexes, owner-shared kitchen/bath units, owner-occupied ADU properties, university housing and nonprofit co-ops are exempt.

rules.title: Berkeley Municipal Code Chapter 13.78 (Tenant Screening and Application Fees)
rules.requirement: Owners who charge a credit-report/application processing fee must give a clear tenant screening fee rights statement and the state fee cap before receiving the fee. Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy or to remove or add a roommate. The chapter applies to all residential rental agreements despite contrary lease terms.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental property in Berkeley.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rent control applies to fully covered units, such as most multifamily units built before 1980, pre-1996 single-family tenancies and rooming houses. Newer construction (CO after June 1980), post-1996 single-family tenancies, most condominiums and certain subsidized units are registered but not rent controlled.
rules.key_value: AGA capped at 5% maximum (CPI-based formula); 65% of Bay Area CPI change; 1.0% for 2026 (CPI 1.5% for Jul 1, 2024 - Jun 30, 2025)
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent control applies to fully covered units such as most multifamily buildings built before 1980.
rules.exemptions: Newer construction, post-1995 single-family tenancies, condominiums, certain subsidized units, golden duplexes, shared-kitchen units, owner-occupied ADU properties, dormitories and nonprofit co-ops are not rent controlled.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection or other decisions, including refusing to rent, demanding higher deposits or rent, or refusing to add family members. Any adverse action based on criminal history requires written notice and an opportunity to respond.
rules.key_value: Administrative fines of $1,000 to $10,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental housing providers in Berkeley with respect to current and prospective tenants.
rules.exemptions: Exempts owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units, lifetime sex offenders, limited public housing/Section 8 cases, owner move-back rental agreements, and existing tenants subletting or adding roommates.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

rules.title: California Civil Code section 1950.5 (Security deposits for residential rental property)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security above one month's rent (two months for small natural-person landlords with no more than two properties and four units; not applicable to service members). The landlord must hold the security for the tenant, offer an initial inspection, take photographs, and return it with an itemized statement within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates.
rules.key_value: Maximum one month's rent (two months for small landlords); return within 21 calendar days; 1 month's rent (2 months for small landlords); Statutory damages up to twice the amount of the security for bad faith
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to California residential landlords generally.
rules.exemptions: Small landlords owning two properties with no more than four units total may charge up to two months' rent.
rules.quoted_span: (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

rules.title: California Civil Code section 1946.2 (Tenant Protection Act just cause)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without just cause stated in the written notice. No-fault terminations require relocation assistance or a final-month rent waiver equal to one month's rent, and a non-compliant notice is void.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months of occupancy; no-fault relocation equals one month's rent, paid within 15 calendar days of notice
rules.exemptions: Exempts transient hotels, care facilities, dormitories, owner-shared housing, owner-occupied single-family and duplex properties, housing with a certificate of occupancy within 15 years, separately alienable homes with non-corporate owners, and deed-restricted affordable housing.
rules.interaction: Yields to a stricter local rule where one applies.
rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

rules.title: State rent increase notice requirement
rules.requirement: State law requires landlords to give 30 days' written advance notice of rent increases of less than 10%.
rules.key_value: 30 days' written notice for increases under 10%
rules.quoted_span: State law requires landlords to provide 30 days' written advance notice of rent increases of less than 10%.

rules.title: California Civil Code section 1950.6 (application screening fees)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee no greater than actual out-of-pocket costs plus reasonable time value, capped at $30 per applicant (CPI-adjusted since 1998). No fee may be charged when no unit is or will be available, and the landlord must give an itemized receipt, process applications in order or refund the fee, and return unused amounts.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, adjustable annually with CPI from January 1, 1998; Maximum screening fee $68.96 for 2026; $30 per applicant, adjusted annually for CPI from Jan 1, 1998
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords of residential rental property and their agents charging applicants screening fees.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.

rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate a tenancy without just cause (at-fault reasons or specified no-fault reasons). No-fault evictions require relocation assistance, and eviction notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service.
rules.key_value: Eligible tenant $11,000 or $14,400; qualified tenant $23,150 or $27,400 (1 Jul 2026 to 30 Jun 2027); one month's rent for qualifying natural-person single-family owners
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers most Los Angeles residential rentals not regulated by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, including single-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Exempts transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity/sorority houses, owner's roommate, some cooperatives, some nonprofit facilities and some government-owned properties.
rules.interaction: A state rule of this category yields to this local rule.
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) – Legal Reasons for Eviction
rules.requirement: RSO units may be evicted only for listed at-fault or no-fault reasons. No-fault evictions require a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict, 30- and 60-day written notice (some 120 days or longer), and relocation assistance; eviction notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days.
rules.key_value: Eviction notices filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service; Eligible tenant $11,000 (under 3 years) or $14,400 (3+ years or low income); qualified tenant $23,150 or $27,400; for 1 Jul 2026 to 30 Jun 2027; Eligible tenant $11,000 (under 3 years) or $14,400 (3+ years or low income); qualified tenant $23,150 or $27,400; for 1 Jul 2026 to 30 Jun 2027, increasing each July 1
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to units subject to the RSO.
rules.interaction: A state rule of this category yields to this local rule.
rules.quoted_span:
All notices to terminate a tenancy for all rental units subject to

) must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) within
three (3) business days of service on the tenant
per Los Angeles Municipal Code 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5.

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance (relocation for demolition for new construction)
rules.requirement: Owners demolishing Protected Units for new construction must pay enhanced relocation to lower income tenants under the RPO and the state Housing Crisis Act, whichever is higher. Tenants also have rights to remain up to 6 months, return and first refusal.
rules.key_value: Standardized payment $115,480 extremely low, $96,750 very low, $87,450 low income; 1 Jul 2026 to 30 Jun 2027
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies only to Protected Units being demolished for new construction.
rules.interaction: A state rule of this category yields to this local rule.
rules.quoted_span:
Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for the purpose of new construction within 5 years after the 
filing of the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD are required to 
comply with relocation requirements under the RPO. Failure to comply with the RPO may result in 
financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.

rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.requirement: Rent for covered units may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable annual percentage set by the city; rent may go to market rate after certain vacancies/evictions. Additional increases require LAHD approval through specific programs.
rules.key_value: One increase per 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage (figure in linked PDF); 3% for 1 Jul 2025 to 30 Jun 2026
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units in buildings first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units.
rules.exemptions: Condominiums and townhomes are not rent-regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995.

rules.title: California Civil Code 1947.12 (Tenant Protection Act rent cap, as added by SB 567)
rules.requirement: An owner of residential real property may not raise the gross rental rate more than 5 percent plus the local percentage change in cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, with no more than two increments in that period. The initial rent for a new tenancy is not capped.
rules.key_value: 5% plus CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rentals statewide, other than the listed exempt categories.
rules.exemptions: Exempts deed-restricted affordable housing, dormitories, housing under stricter local rent control, housing with a certificate of occupancy within 15 years, certain separately alienable homes with non-corporate owners, and owner-occupied duplexes.
rules.interaction: Yields to a stricter local rule where one applies.
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Bans selling, licensing or providing an algorithmic device (software using nonpublic competitor data to recommend rents or occupancy) to a landlord, and bans landlords from using one to set rental rates or occupancy levels. Excludes aggregated reports from public or 90+ day-old data and affordable housing program tools. Tenants may sue for remedies.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each property is a separate violation; Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental property in the City of San Diego regardless of building age or size.
rules.exemptions: Excludes software that publishes aggregated reports from public or historical data and software used to set rents under affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.citation: San Diego Municipal Code Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 11, §§98.1101-98.1104 (O-2025-107)
rules.quoted_span:
It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an
algorithmic device to a landlord.
(b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.

rules.title: Residential Tenant Protections (Tenants' Right to Know Regulations), San Diego Municipal Code Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without at-fault or no-fault just cause. No-fault grounds (owner or relative occupancy, withdrawal from the market, government orders, demolition or substantial remodel) carry notice, proof, re-rental and relocation-assistance duties. Landlords must give tenants a written notice of protections and the Tenant Protection Guide.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; owner move-in for at least 12 continuous months, occupant must move in within 90 days; remodel requires vacating at least 30 continuous days; Relocation assistance: 2 months' actual rent (3 months if tenant is senior or disabled); no-fault notice 30 or 60 days; offer-to-renew right for 5 years; Relocation assistance of 2 months' rent (3 months for seniors 62+ or disabled tenants) for no-fault terminations
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental tenancies in San Diego unless exempt.
rules.exemptions: Exempts new construction under 15 years old, certain owner-occupied and separately alienable housing, affordable and subsidised housing, hotels, dormitories, care facilities and mobilehomes under state law.
rules.interaction: A state rule of this category yields to this local rule.
rules.citation: San Diego Municipal Code §§98.0701-98.0705 (Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7)
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.

rules.title: Section 37.10C of the Rent Ordinance
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. A tenant or the City Attorney may bring a civil action over violations.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential units in San Francisco.
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of such algorithmic devices and allows a tenant or the City Attorney to bring a civil action if they believe an entity is in violation of the law.

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Board – Security Deposit Interest Rate
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay interest on tenant security deposits at the rate set by the Rent Board. The rate for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027 is 4.2%.
rules.key_value: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
rules.quoted_span: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance Section 37.9(a) (Just Cause Evictions)
rules.requirement: A landlord of a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance may evict only for one of 17 listed just causes that is the dominant motive; expiration of a rental agreement or change in ownership is not just cause. Just cause is also needed to remove housing services, and some tenancies exempt from rent increase limits (e.g., certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979) remain subject to the eviction provisions.
rules.key_value: 17 just cause reasons under Section 37.9(a); Owner move-in etc. (notices served 3/01/26–2/28/27): $8,245 per tenant, max $24,733 per unit, plus $5,497 per elderly/disabled tenant or household with minor child. Ellis Act (same period): $11,110.05 per tenant, max $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 per elderly (62+) or disabled tenant.; Sec. 37.9C for notices served 3/1/26–2/28/27: $8,245 per tenant, max $24,733 per unit, plus $5,497 per elderly/disabled tenant or household with minor child; Ellis Act (37.9A): $11,110.05 per tenant, max $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 per elderly/disabled tenant; temporary displacement under 20 days: $446/day plus actual moving expenses
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance, including newly constructed units and Costa-Hawkins-exempt tenancies for eviction purposes.
rules.interaction: A state rule of this category yields to this local rule.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance – Allowable Annual Rent Increase
rules.requirement: Landlords of units covered by the Rent Ordinance may raise rent annually by no more than the allowable percentage set by the Rent Board. The rate for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
rules.key_value: 1.6% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027; 1.6% for 1 Mar 2026 to 28 Feb 2027 (1.4% for 1 Mar 2025 to 28 Feb 2026)
rules.interaction: A state rule of this category yields to this local rule.
rules.quoted_span: 1.6% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

rules.title: Santa Ana algorithmic rent-setting software ordinance
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental properties in Santa Ana. Does not apply to pricing software relying solely on publicly available data, aggregate historical data, or tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements. Tenants may sue directly and need only prove use of the prohibited technology, not intentional collusion.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to software using only public or aggregate historical data, or tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements.
rules.citation: Santa Ana algorithmic rent-setting software ordinance (no ordinance number given)
rules.quoted_span: The ordinance, approved on Tuesday, Feb. 17, for a first reading and set for a final vote on March 3, prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental properties.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days, an owner may not terminate a tenancy without just cause stated in a written notice, and must first give notice and time to cure at-fault violations. For no-fault terminations the owner must provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive the last 3 months of rent.
rules.key_value: 3 months relocation assistance or 3 months rent waiver for no-fault termination
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental housing generally.
rules.exemptions: Exempts housing produced in the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, hotels and transient occupancy, hospital and care facilities, dormitories and other shared living quarters.
rules.interaction: A state rule of this category yields to this local rule.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.

rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.requirement: Residential rent increases are limited to the lower of 3% per year or 80% of the CPI change over the most recent 12 months; no increase if CPI is negative. Owners may petition for relief and must give written notice of the ordinance at lease start or with any rent increase notice.
rules.key_value: Lower of 3% or 80% of CPI change over 12 months; no increase if CPI negative; Lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change; 2.87% for 1 Sep 2026 to 31 Aug 2027
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers residential rental buildings constructed on or before February 1, 1995.
rules.exemptions: Buildings constructed after February 1, 1995 and mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990 are exempt.
rules.interaction: A state rule of this category yields to this local rule.
rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.

rules.title: California Government Code section 12955 (Housing Discrimination; source of income)
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not discriminate based on source of income, including government rent subsidies and vouchers. Where a government rent subsidy applies, income standards must be based on the tenant's portion of rent, and applicants must be allowed to offer alternative evidence of ability to pay instead of credit history. Inquiring about the level or source of income is not discrimination.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to owners of housing accommodations generally.
rules.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: A landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal. They must also send a copy of the notice, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the Office of Housing Stability. The requirements cannot be waived.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources delivered with the Notice to Quit; Fine of $300 per day for second and subsequent offenses
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in Boston.
rules.exemptions: Exempt are residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities.
rules.quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement. The Notice of
Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to
Quit.

rules.title: Boston Fair Housing Regulations
rules.requirement: Landlords in Boston may not discriminate against renters based on rental assistance, such as Section 8, social security disability or veterans vouchers. Refusing to accept rental assistance is treated as housing discrimination.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing rentals, sales and financing in the City of Boston.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord tells you they don't accept rental assistance.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.requirement: Housing providers receiving DND funding or land, or with BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units, may not use blanket bans on applicants with arrests or convictions and must not consider non-conviction arrests, judicially relieved convictions, juvenile records, or convictions over 5 years old (except with a direct relationship to the housing or unreasonable risk to others). Credit scores may not be used to approve or deny applications; credit history may be used only in lieu of rental history.
rules.key_value: No consideration of convictions more than 5 years old; no use of credit scores
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing receiving DND funding or land or inclusionary income-restricted units.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing or unreasonable risk to others, or to current criminal behavior; conflicting federal or state law preempts.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, February 2017)
rules.quoted_span:
Housing providers will consider applicants on 
a case-by-case basis.

rules.title: City Council policy order on algorithmic rent-pricing software
rules.requirement: The council directed the city manager to work with city departments to draft policy options or ordinance language banning residential property management companies from contracting with firms that use algorithmic or AI-driven models to recommend rents. No ban is in force yet.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would apply to residential property management companies that use algorithmic pricing services.
rules.citation: Cambridge City Council policy order (June 2026), no number given
rules.quoted_span: City council also unanimously passed a policy order initiating steps to ban residential property management companies from contracting companies that use algorithmic and AI-driven models to recommend what they should charge for rent.

rules.title: Tenants Rights and Resources Ordinance (Chapter 8.71, Cambridge Municipal Code)
rules.requirement: Owners, landlords and management companies must give tenants a city Guide on housing rights and resources at the start of a tenancy and when legal steps to terminate it are taken (e.g., Notice to Quit or Summary Process). It does not bar evictions otherwise allowed by law.
rules.key_value: Guide provided at tenancy start and at termination; fine of $300 per day of violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental agreements, including a single residential dwelling unit and tenants at will.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to hospital, skilled nursing or health facility units, non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities, or short term rental units.
rules.citation: Chapter 8.71 of the Cambridge Municipal Code
rules.quoted_span: The Ordinance also requires that a landlord provide the Guide to tenants when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken (ex. Notice to Quit or Summary Process).

rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance, chapter 14.04
rules.requirement: Landlords, sellers and rental agents may screen applicants only by reasonable standards applied equally and uniformly, such as ability to pay rent and ability to care for the apartment. Discrimination based on protected categories, including source of income (Section 8 and public benefits), is prohibited.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing rental and sales transactions in Cambridge.
rules.exemptions: Two-family dwellings where the owner lives are exempt.
rules.quoted_span: Under the law, landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.

rules.title: General Laws Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 15B
rules.requirement: A lessor may require at or before tenancy start only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of no more than first month's rent, and the cost of a key and lock. Deposits must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, earn 5% interest (or the lesser bank rate) annually, and be returned within 30 days of the tenancy ending, less permitted deductions with an itemized sworn list. A statement of condition and receipts are required.
rules.key_value: Security deposit capped at 1 month's rent; interest 5% per year; return within 30 days
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property leases and tenancies.
rules.quoted_span: (iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2);

rules.title: General Laws Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 12 - Notice to determine estate at will
rules.requirement: Tenancies at will may be ended by either party with three months' written notice, or the rent-payment interval or 30 days if longer when rent is payable at intervals under three months. For nonpayment of rent, 14 days' written notice to quit suffices, but the tenant may stop termination by paying all rent due within 10 days if no similar notice was received in the prior 12 months, and the notice must include a prescribed statement of that right.
rules.key_value: 3 months' notice (or rent interval/30 days if longer); 14 days' notice for nonpayment; 10-day right to cure; 14 days' written notice to quit; Damages of 1 to 3 months' rent or actual damages, whichever is greater; 6-month rebuttable presumption
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenancies at will.
rules.citation: General Law - Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 12
rules.quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and, if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer.

rules.title: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
rules.requirement: Would authorize the city of Boston to implement tenant eviction protections. The bill text is not shown in this chunk, so the specific grounds and duties are not stated.
rules.quoted_span: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections

rules.title: 254 CMR 7 (broker regulations on fees to prospective tenants)
rules.requirement: Licensed brokers may charge fees to prospective tenants if they give written notice of the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on a lease. The notice must be given at the first personal meeting and signed by the applicant, with any refusal recorded.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to licensed brokers dealing with prospective tenants.
rules.quoted_span: In addition to holding a valid license, the broker has to tell the applicant in writing the amount of the broker’s fee, the time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on the owner and applicant actually entering into a lease or rental agreement.

rules.title: General Laws Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 15B (upfront charges)
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, no lessor or agent may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay more than first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent, and the cost of a key and lock. Lessors must give receipts for advance payments. A fee in lieu of a deposit may be authorized by regulation, capped at one month's rent in total.
rules.key_value: Upfront payments limited to first month, last month, deposit of 1 month, and key/lock cost; Only first, last, security deposit and lock change may be charged upfront
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property leases and tenancies.
rules.quoted_span: (b) At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:

rules.title: General Laws Chapter 112, Section 87DDD 1/2 (Real estate brokers and salesmen; persons finding dwelling accommodations for fee)
rules.requirement: Only licensed brokers or salespersons may find dwelling accommodations for tenants for a fee. From August 1, 2025, a broker may contract solely with either the tenant or the landlord, and any fee must be paid only by the party who originally engaged the broker.
rules.key_value: Broker fee payable only by the party who engaged the broker
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to brokers and persons finding rental dwellings for a fee, and to the parties who engage them.
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21, An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases
rules.requirement: Would have repealed the state ban on rent control and capped annual rent increases statewide for most residential rental units. The SJC held in Cella v. Attorney General that the petition could not appear on the November 2026 ballot.
rules.key_value: Lesser of annual CPI increase or 5%
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental units statewide.
rules.exemptions: Exempts owner-occupied buildings of four or fewer units, units under 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious or nonprofit purposes.
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%.

rules.title: General Laws Part I, Title VII, Chapter 40P, Section 4 (General prohibition; exception)
rules.requirement: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind. A municipality that accepts the chapter may adopt only voluntary rent control that excludes regulation of occupancy, services, evictions and condominium conversion, excludes owners of fewer than ten units and units with fair market rent over $400, and requires the municipality to compensate owners from general funds.
rules.key_value: Rent control barred; narrow exception: voluntary after six months, owners of fewer than ten units and units over $400 fair market rent excluded, municipality compensates owners
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all cities and towns and to rental housing generally.
rules.citation: General Laws Part I, Title VII, Chapter 40P, Section 4
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:

rules.title: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
rules.requirement: Would authorize the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization. The bill text is not shown in this chunk, so no cap or formula is stated.
rules.quoted_span: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections

rules.title: M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10) – Discrimination against recipients of public assistance or housing subsidies
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for anyone furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against an individual because they receive federal, state or local public assistance or housing subsidies (including rental assistance), or because of any requirement of such a program.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person furnishing rental accommodations, with no exemptions stated in this subsection.
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient, or because of any requirement of such public assistance, rental assistance, or housing subsidy program.

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Makes it an unlawful antitrust violation for rental property owners to pay for or use a coordinator's services, for coordinators to facilitate rent-fixing agreements, for anyone to engage in parallel pricing coordination, or for any person to perform a coordinating function (algorithmic setting or recommending of rents, lease terms or occupancy using competitors' nonpublic information). Municipalities may not enact conflicting ordinances.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental residential dwelling units in New Jersey and to the owners and coordinators who set or recommend their rents.
rules.exemptions: Excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care and detention facilities, and government setting rents through affordability controls.
rules.interaction: Its text bars conflicting local ordinances; flagged for review.
rules.quoted_span: any person to perform a coordinating function.

rules.title: New Jersey Security Deposit Law
rules.requirement: Landlords may collect a security deposit of at most 1.5 times one month's rent, with yearly increases capped at 10% of the current deposit. Deposits are held in trust in interest-bearing accounts, interest belongs to the tenant, and the landlord must give written notice of the bank, amount and rate.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent maximum; annual increase at most 10% of current deposit; Return within 30 days of termination; 5 business days if displaced by fire, flood or condemnation; 7% per annum if notice or interest is not provided
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant requests application 30 days after written request.
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less.

rules.title: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act
rules.requirement: Eligible senior, disabled or disabled-veteran tenants in buildings being converted to condominium or cooperative ownership may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their income is within the limit. Landlords or converters must notify tenants of their right to apply.
rules.key_value: 40 years of protection; income limit of 3 times county average per person income or $50,000, whichever is greater
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to eligible tenants in converted buildings.
rules.quoted_span:
Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years 
if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their 
county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28).

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act of 1992
rules.requirement: Extends protected tenancy against eviction to qualified tenants in converted buildings who were not eligible as seniors or disabled persons. The only qualified county is currently Hudson County.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to qualified tenants in Hudson County converted buildings.
rules.quoted_span:
The Tenant Protection Law of 1992 amendment extends protections to qualified tenants in 
qualified counties in buildings converted or being converted who were not eligible for Protected 
Tenancy as either Senior Citizens or Disabled Persons under the “Senior Citizens and Disabled 
Protected Tenancy Act of 1981” (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.40 to -61.59; N.J.A.C. 5:24-3.1 to -3.4).

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act
rules.requirement: A landlord may recover possession of a residential unit only by consent or through court eviction, and must have good cause (statutory grounds). Each cause except nonpayment must be described in a written notice, and a Notice to Quit is required for all good cause evictions except nonpayment; the landlord may not evict or refuse to renew a lease without good cause.
rules.key_value: Warrant for possession not issued until 3 business days after judgment; tenant has 3 business days to move; Notice to Quit from 3 days up to 3 years depending on the ground; 18 months for permanent retirement from residential use; 3 years for condominium conversion; relocation assistance of six times monthly rent for illegal occupancy; 3-month, 1-month or 3-day notice to quit depending on tenancy and cause; 6-month owner occupancy; 5-year bar on residential use
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rentals including single-family homes, mobile homes, apartment buildings, and rooming and boarding homes.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to certain owner-occupied two- or three-unit premises, transient or seasonal guests, or a unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord must have 
good cause to evict a tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53). There are several grounds for a good cause 
eviction.

rules.title: Reprisal law (civil rights of tenants)
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot retaliate against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of lease terms or refusal to renew when the tenant exercises certain rights, such as enforcing lease rights, making good-faith complaints or organizing. A tenant may sue for damages.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are excluded.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of 
a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A. 
2A:42-10.10).

rules.title: New Jersey Foreclosure Fairness Act
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction. Before evicting a tenant of a foreclosed property bought by an owner-occupant, the landlord must give a 90-day notice to quit. The new owner must give notices in English and Spanish within 10 business days after the sale, and any offer to vacate must be voluntary and free of pressure tactics.
rules.key_value: 90-day notice to quit; notice to tenants within 10 business days of sale
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants of foreclosed residential rental property.
rules.quoted_span:
Before a tenant can be evicted due 
to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90 -day notice to qui t when the 
foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her 
primary residence.

rules.title: P.L. 2025, c.405 (Residential rental property application fee not to exceed $50)
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property that exceeds $50. The cap is adjusted annually by CPI change; any amount wrongfully charged is remitted to the applicant from the collected penalty.
rules.key_value: $50 cap, adjusted annually for CPI (NY-Northern NJ-Long Island area) when the change is above zero
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords and their agents charging application fees for residential rentals.
rules.exemptions: Exempts units in one- or two-family dwellings and NJ Real Estate Commission licensees who are not the landlord.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.

rules.title: City of Hoboken algorithmic rent-fixing ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords renting residential units in Hoboken may not use software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels among competing landlords.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords renting residential units in Hoboken.
rules.interaction: A state rule of this category bars conflicting local ordinances; flagged for review.
rules.citation: City of Hoboken outlaws algorithmic rent-fixing (City Council meeting of July 9, 2025)
rules.quoted_span: It will now be illegal for landlords renting residential units in Hoboken to engage in price-fixing through algorithmic rent-fixing, meaning they can no longer use software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels among competing landlords.

rules.title: Rent Control Ordinance, Chapter 260 of the Jersey City Municipal Code
rules.requirement: Jersey City administers and enforces a rent control ordinance that regulates rent in covered buildings, including landlord applications for rent increases (capital improvement, hardship) and tenant petitions over illegal rent. All 1-4 unit properties are exempt.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental properties with five or more units.
rules.exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties are exempt; other exemptions may be requested through a Rent Control Exemption Request.
rules.interaction: A state rule of this category bars conflicting local ordinances; flagged for review.
rules.citation: Chapter 260 of the Jersey City Municipal Code
rules.quoted_span: (Please Note: All 1-4 Unit Properties are exempt from rent control)

rules.title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control ordinances for 30 years after completion of construction. New Jersey has no state rent control, and municipalities may adopt rent control.
rules.key_value: 30-year exemption from local rent control
rules.coverage_conditions: Exempts newly constructed multiple dwellings from local rent control.
rules.exemptions: Buildings less than 30 years since completion are exempt from local rent control; government-subsidized rents may also be exempt.
rules.interaction: Its text bars conflicting local ordinances; flagged for review.
rules.quoted_span:
Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly 
constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period 
of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.

rules.title: Rent increases barred for conversion costs (Anti-Eviction Act, conversion provision)
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion. Rents may still be raised to cover the cost of new services or amenities, and the bar protects all tenants regardless of senior or disabled protected-tenancy status.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to buildings converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple unit ownership.
rules.quoted_span:
If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee 
simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the 
conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).

rules.title: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (source of lawful income)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or discriminate in rental on protected bases including source of lawful income. Landlords may still refuse applicants for insufficient income or poor credit history.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all landlord-tenant relationships except specified exemptions.
rules.exemptions: Excludes two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in owner-occupied single homes, and certain single-sex or age-restricted housing.
rules.quoted_span:
The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), 
N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires 
equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, 
ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, 
affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, 
nationality, or source of lawful income.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about an applicant's criminal record until after a conditional offer. They may never consider arrests without conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated, juvenile or sealed records. After an offer they may consider only listed serious convictions or recent convictions within look-back periods, and must do an individualized assessment and give written reasons if they withdraw the offer.
rules.key_value: Look-back after conditional offer: 6 years (first-degree), 4 years (second/third-degree), 1 year (fourth-degree); serious listed offenses with no limit
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental dwelling units offered for rent by housing providers.
rules.exemptions: Excludes dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.quoted_span:
A housing
provider
shall not make any oral or written inquiry
regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
